_note: HAND-AUTHORED source for the book's LITERATURE-POSITIONING model — the Literature-Positioning Pass (LPP) as a typed, checkable object. One record per intervention (a place the book positions itself against prior/adjacent work), each carrying the editorial X->Y->Z frame the pass mandates: X (established lineage), Y (current frontier), Z (the narrow MAGE move). This file IS edited by hand; lit-positioning.json is generated from it (`python3 book-models/lit_positioning_model.py regenerate`). Mirrors the flagship_stack / argument_spine declared-source->generated-artifact shape. WHY A NEW MODEL, NOT AN EXTENSION: the argument-spine holds the book's own ordered claims; the claims model holds unordered stances. A literature-positioning intervention is neither — it is a place where the book SITUATES itself against OUTSIDE work, carrying fields no sibling holds: the X/Y/Z lineage frame, the target chapter locations, and — the load-bearing addition — CITATIONS AS MODELED OBJECTS nested under the spine. Each entry in a record's `citations` is not a bare bib key but `{key, backs_claims[], relation}`: `key` = the references.bib key; `backs_claims[]` = the argument-spine claim id(s) this citation substantiates or situates (the join that nests the literature UNDER the spine, so a spine claim can be reached from its backing literature); `relation` in {substantiates (direct empirical support), situates (positions MAGE against the lineage/frontier), corroborates (independent convergence), convergent-evidence (practitioner report, NOT establishing)}. This layer + the data-claim ledger are the two halves the substantiation aggregator joins under each spine claim to flag under-substantiated-or-situated reality-claims. The LP1-LP6 conformance check holds the frame mechanically and lands AUDIT-ONLY-FIRST (reports, does not gate). `status` (planned|landed) is the LPP burndown signal: landed means the X->Y->Z passage + its citations are in the book (LP3 confirms every landed citation resolves in references.bib AND appears in a target chapter); planned means the intervention is modeled but not yet written (its citations may be planned keys not yet in the .bib — LP3 reports those as pending, never a failure). `fold_target` names the wave a folded intervention lands within (W7 / W5 / W5-Part5); "" for a standalone wave. Verb discipline (from the LPP instructions): "shows"/substantiates for direct empirical findings only; practitioner build-reports are convergent-evidence, never "establish". §7 (architecture conformance) is deliberately absent — the author handles it separately.

interventions.title: Human oversight / review saturation
interventions.x: Human review has long been the accepted safeguard on machine-generated changes.
interventions.y: At agent throughput, per-change oversight becomes emergent, effortful work that does not keep pace — Dhanorkar et al. document 17 developers doing four forms of oversight.
interventions.z: MAGE spends human attention per class of failure, encoded as a mechanism the environment enforces, not per individual change.
interventions.notes: STANDALONE wave. Claim CONFIRMED: interviews with 17 developers surface four forms of emergent oversight (a priori control, co-planning, real-time monitoring, post hoc review). Title-case rendering is a choice, not an error (arXiv renders sentence-case). Key dhanorkar2026oversight (arXiv 2606.05391) planned — not yet in references.bib.

interventions.title: Harness engineering (environment supersets weights)
interventions.x: Foundation-model capability has been read off the model weights.
interventions.y: Recent work locates coding-agent capability in the runtime harness — tools, middleware, memory — more than the prompt; Lin et al. ablate the gain to tools/middleware/long-term memory, not the system prompt.
interventions.z: MAGE treats the harness as ONE layer of a governed environment, not a synonym for it — the environment encodes obligations the harness alone does not.

interventions.title: Persistent context / code-graphs
interventions.x: Agents lose the codebase between turns; the working context must be reconstructed each time.
interventions.y: Recent systems give agents a persistent, queryable representation of the repository — code graphs and codebase memory (RepoGraph, CodexGraph, Codebase-Memory, RANGER).
interventions.z: MAGE makes the models themselves the persistent context: the typed model IS the compact representation agents reason through and engineers specify against.

interventions.title: Spec-driven agentic development
interventions.x: Specifications have always framed what software must do.
interventions.y: Spec-driven development places an authoritative spec/contract around a stochastic generator with deterministic validation; academic studies show specification quality, not model capability, is the success factor (Vilas Boas et al.) and that citation-to-spec discipline enables 86-88% hallucination detection (Panda).
interventions.z: MAGE binds intent into drift-checked models — the spec is not a document but an enforced, executable model the environment holds implementation to.
interventions.notes: = W-SDD. Core LANDED (W-SDD c2225e0); the blog cite sdd-abdurrahman-2026 resolves in references.bib and appears in 3.1-the-executable-zoo. interventions.title: Deterministic verification / trusted checkers
interventions.x: Formal verification gives machine-checked guarantees but at heavy human cost (Ringer et al., QED at Large).
interventions.y: Recent work pairs an untrusted LLM generator with a trusted checker or prover — kernel-checked admission (AutoSOUP; AutoRocq; Fang & Xiong's ITP-checked project generation).
interventions.z: MAGE preserves the guarantee boundary: the stochastic generator proposes, a deterministic mechanism admits — the environment enforces the check, not the agent.

interventions.title: SWE-Bench / fallible oracles
interventions.x: A passing test suite has stood in for requirement satisfaction; automated repair long showed patches overfit the visible suite (Smith et al.).
interventions.y: The frontier now governs the oracle itself — OpenAI retiring SWE-Bench Verified (59.4% flawed test cases), decontaminated and live successors (Scale AI's SWE-Bench Pro at ~23%; the SWE-Bench Illusion 76%->53% memorization signature; SWE-bench-Live), and evidence that agent-authored tests are over-mocked or implementation-coupled (Hora & Robbes; the oracle study).
interventions.z: MAGE treats the suite as a fallible model that must be governed: completion is re-derived from the artifact and multiple evidence sources, not read off a green bar.

interventions.title: Engineer role / SE-education
interventions.x: Software engineering has always been more than typing code.
interventions.y: Empirical study finds AI assistants recomposing developer work toward supervision (Vella & Blincoe: 82% report writing less code; they name it 'supervisory engineering work'), and education begins teaching critique and responsible GenAI use (Jackson/Liu/van der Hoek).
interventions.z: MAGE describes where the seat moves — human effort concentrates on intent, architecture, model authorship, validation, and judgment — not that coding is obsolete.
interventions.notes: STANDALONE wave. Frame: 'the seat moves', NOT 'coding obsolete'. Vella & Blincoe = supervisory engineering work (empirical, longitudinal, N=158/95 completing both phases). Jackson et al. = SE-education centered on design, critique, responsible use. vella2026impact (2605.23135) + jackson2025genaidesign (2506.21703) planned, not yet in the .bib.

interventions.title: Deep single-case methodology
interventions.x: The single-case field report is a recognized method — case-study guidelines and mechanism-based process-tracing generalization (Runeson & Höst; Beach & Pedersen).
interventions.y: Practitioner build-reports now document large agentic builds (Cloudflare vinext, ~1 week / 1 engineer / ~$1,100; Anthropic's C compiler — 16 agents, a ~100K-line Rust compiler building Linux 6.9 on x86/ARM/RISC-V; Anthropic/Bun's million-line Zig->Rust migration) and a governable-agentic case study (Davis et al., Cheap Code, Costly Judgment).
interventions.z: MAGE grounds its method in one deep case (DocAble), motivating hypotheses for broader use — a field report, never a proof.
